name: At
description: Adversaries may abuse the at utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code. The at utility exists as an executable within Windows, Linux, and macOS for scheduling tasks at a specified time and date. Although deprecated in favor of Scheduled Task's schtasks in Windows environments, using at requires that the Task Scheduler service be running, and the user to be logged on as a member of the local Administrators group. In addition to explicitly running the `at` command, adversaries may also schedule a task with at by directly leveraging the Windows Management Instrumentation `Win32_ScheduledJob` WMI class. On Linux and macOS, at may be invoked by the superuser as well as any users added to the at.allow file. If the at.allow file does not exist, the at.deny file is checked. Every username not listed in at.deny is allowed to invoke at. If the at.deny exists and is empty, global use of at is permitted. If neither file exists (which is often the baseline) only the superuser is allowed to use at. Adversaries may use at to execute programs at system startup or on a scheduled basis for Persistence. at can also be abused to conduct remote Execution as part of Lateral Movement and/or to run a process under the context of a specified account (such as SYSTEM). In Linux environments, adversaries may also abuse at to break out of restricted environments by using a task to spawn an interactive system shell or to run system commands. Similarly, at may also be used for Privilege Escalation if the binary is allowed to run as superuser via sudo.

detection.condition: s1_process_action_create and ((s2_at_exe_path and s3_at_command_line_time_pattern and s4_at_command_line_command_keywords) or (s5_wmic_powershell_exe_path and s6_wmi_scheduled_job_cmdline and s7_wmi_scheduled_job_create_action))

operational_usage: SOC 팀은 이 규칙을 활용하여 'at' 유틸리티 또는 WMI 'Win32_ScheduledJob' 클래스를 이용한 악성 작업 스케줄링 시도를 탐지할 수 있습니다. 'at.exe'의 직접 실행 시에는 특정 시간 패턴과 함께 의심스러운 명령줄 인자를 모니터링하고, PowerShell 또는 WMIC를 통한 WMI 'Win32_ScheduledJob' 생성 시도를 탐지합니다. 탐지된 이벤트는 높은 심각도로 분류되어 즉각적인 알람을 트리거하고, 관련 프로세스 및 예약된 작업에 대한 추가적인 포렌식 조사를 시작하는 데 사용될 수 있습니다. 특히, 지속성, 권한 상승 또는 원격 코드 실행 전술과 결합될 때 중요도가 더욱 높아집니다.
false_positive: 정상적인 시스템 관리 도구, 스크립트, 또는 합법적인 애플리케이션이 'at' 명령이나 WMI 'Win32_ScheduledJob'을 사용하여 합법적인 작업을 예약하는 경우 오탐이 발생할 수 있습니다. 알려진 정상적인 예약 작업 패턴, 특정 프로세스, 또는 WMI 호출에 대해 화이트리스트를 적용하여 오탐을 줄일 수 있습니다.
